nodes.title: Error Taxonomy
nodes.summary: Define a small stable taxonomy separating client or domain failures, dependency failures, and programmer or invariant failures with machine-readable codes. This prevents unsafe retries and misleading responses.
nodes.probe: Parse error declarations and transport mappings; assert distinct machine-readable categories exist for validation, domain, dependency, and internal failures, and that each exported code maps to exactly one public status and retry policy.

nodes.title: Typed Domain Errors
nodes.summary: Use typed errors or discriminated result values at service boundaries and map them explicitly to transport responses. This prevents brittle string matching and accidental conversion of actionable failures into generic or successful results.
nodes.probe: Run a static AST check over exported service functions; require a typed result or declared error type, flag string-only error comparisons, and verify each declared variant has an explicit transport mapping.

nodes.title: Error Cause Preservation
nodes.summary: Wrap lower-level failures with operation context while preserving the original cause, stack, retryability, and safe classification. This keeps root causes actionable across repository, transport, and queue boundaries.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect representative repository, dependency, queue, and transport wrappers and confirm that each adds operation context, retains the original cause and stack, preserves retry classification, and sanitizes only at the public boundary.

nodes.title: Exception Boundaries
nodes.summary: Catch exceptions only at intentional request, worker, CLI, or process boundaries and translate them once. This prevents duplicate logs, inconsistent status mapping, and lower layers deciding how callers recover.
nodes.probe: Enumerate catch or exception handlers and assert each either rethrows or wraps with a cause or returns a documented boundary response; flag catches inside domain code that translate to transport-specific behavior.

nodes.title: No Swallowed Exceptions
nodes.summary: Prohibit empty catches and catches that only log before returning success, a default value, or a partially applied result. This prevents silent data loss, false acknowledgements, and corrupted downstream state.
nodes.probe: AST-scan catch blocks and fail on empty bodies, bare/default-value returns, or log-only handling without a rethrow or explicit error result; permit only annotated, documented best-effort handlers.

nodes.title: Safe Error Disclosure
nodes.summary: Return stable client-safe errors without stacks, SQL, credentials, or internal paths while retaining a correlation identifier for internal diagnostics. This prevents information disclosure while preserving incident linkage.
nodes.probe: Exercise representative 4xx and 5xx responses and assert no stack, SQL, credential, or filesystem-path patterns occur; then verify internal logs contain the returned correlation identifier without exposing secrets.

nodes.title: Ingress Validation
nodes.summary: Validate every external input at its ingress boundary for required fields, types, ranges, formats, and allowed values before business logic runs. This prevents malformed or hostile data from reaching trusted paths.
nodes.probe: Enumerate HTTP, CLI, queue, webhook, and file handlers and assert each parses a schema before invoking application services; run missing-field, wrong-type, out-of-range, malformed-encoding, and unknown-field fixtures.

nodes.title: Schema Size Limits
nodes.summary: Enforce body, string, array, nesting, upload, and batch-size limits before expensive parsing or allocation. This prevents resource-exhaustion attacks and parser failures from oversized input.
nodes.probe: Send payloads just above each configured body, field, collection, nesting, decompression, and upload limit; assert rejection before handler work with the documented 4xx status and no unbounded allocation.

nodes.title: Canonicalize Once
nodes.summary: Canonicalize encodings, paths, identifiers, and Unicode representations once before validation and authorization, then pass canonical values inward. This prevents alternate representations from bypassing checks or creating duplicate records.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect ingress, authorization, routing, and persistence paths for a single documented normalization point and verify that alternate encodings, Unicode forms, case variants, and traversal representations cannot produce divergent authorization or identity results.

nodes.title: Twelve-Factor Configuration
nodes.summary: Load deploy-varying configuration from the environment or an approved external configuration system rather than checked-in runtime files or source literals. This prevents environment drift, unsafe defaults, and committed credentials.
nodes.probe: Parse deployment manifests and config loaders; fail if deploy-varying values or credentials are literal constants outside test fixtures, or if checked-in config is mutable runtime state rather than injected configuration.

nodes.title: Boot Configuration Validation
nodes.summary: Validate required environment variables, types, ranges, URLs, credentials, and mutually exclusive settings before accepting work. This prevents a misconfigured process from serving partial traffic or consuming jobs.
nodes.probe: Launch the application with each required variable absent and with representative invalid values; assert nonzero exit before it listens or consumes work, and verify diagnostics identify the setting without printing its secret value.

nodes.title: Explicit Configuration Defaults
nodes.summary: Document every configuration default and forbid silent fallback for security, identity, persistence, billing, or data-loss settings. This prevents absent settings from quietly selecting unsafe behavior.
nodes.probe: Present this exact question for each security, identity, persistence, billing, or data-loss setting: “When this setting is absent, which behavior is approved?” Options: “fail startup,” “use the documented safe default,” or “use an explicitly approved fallback with owner and expiry.” Record the selected option and evidence of review.

nodes.title: Secret Storage
nodes.summary: Store secrets only in an approved secret manager or injected runtime secret and grant the narrowest identity, scope, and lifetime that works. This prevents credentials from spreading through source, images, artifacts, developer machines, or overprivileged workloads.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect secret-manager configuration, workload identities, IAM scopes, deployment manifests, image layers, and runtime injection; confirm no plaintext secret is persisted outside approved stores and that access, rotation, and revocation are auditable.

nodes.title: Secret History Scanning
nodes.summary: Scan the working tree, full repository history, generated artifacts, CI logs, and release bundles for secrets, then revoke confirmed exposures. This prevents a removed credential from remaining usable in historical or shipped material.
nodes.probe: Run `gitleaks detect --redact --source . --log-opts=--all` plus artifact and CI-log scans; fail on verified findings and require revocation records for historical hits. Check that detectors inspect all release bundle and image layers.

nodes.title: Secret Redaction
nodes.summary: Redact tokens, passwords, API keys, personal data, and signed URLs from logs, errors, traces, dumps, metrics labels, and request URLs. This prevents observability and support systems from becoming durable credential stores.
nodes.probe: Inject fixture secrets through each logging, tracing, error, dump, metrics, and URL path; assert exact values and recognizable token forms never occur in captured output, including serialized nested fields.

nodes.title: Lockfile Reproducibility
nodes.summary: Commit one authoritative lockfile per package manager and install from it in frozen or immutable mode in CI and release builds. This prevents developers and deploys from resolving different transitive graphs for the same revision.
nodes.probe: Detect the package manager from manifests, require its lockfile in version control, and run a clean temporary-directory frozen install twice; compare dependency checksums and resolved graphs for identity.

nodes.title: Immutable Dependency Pins
nodes.summary: Pin release dependencies to reviewed immutable versions and pin CI or container actions to immutable digests where supported. This prevents mutable ranges or tags from changing production code without review.
nodes.probe: Parse manifests, lockfiles, Dockerfiles, and CI workflows; fail on unbounded ranges, floating tags, or unpinned action references except documented development-only cases.

nodes.title: Dependency Update SLA
nodes.summary: Automate dependency advisories and define owner, severity-based remediation deadlines, and expiry dates for accepted exceptions. This prevents vulnerable or obsolete packages from remaining indefinitely without ownership.
nodes.probe: Parse Dependabot/Renovate configuration and vulnerability reports; assert every production dependency has an owner and every open finding is within its severity SLA or has an unexpired exception.

nodes.title: Dependency Provenance and SBOM
nodes.summary: Record dependency checksums and provenance, publish an SBOM for each release, and review unexpected direct or transitive additions. This prevents compromised mirrors, typosquats, or unreviewed packages entering shipped artifacts unnoticed.
nodes.probe: Generate an SPDX or CycloneDX SBOM from the lockfile, compare it with the previous release, and fail on additions without an owner or provenance evidence; verify listed hashes match the built artifact inputs.

nodes.title: License Policy
nodes.summary: Inventory direct and transitive dependency licenses and enforce an approved policy with required notices and attribution in shipped artifacts. This prevents release-time legal violations from overlooked transitive obligations.
nodes.probe: Generate a lockfile-derived SPDX license report and fail CI for disallowed, unknown, or missing licenses and for absent required notice files; compare the report with the shipped artifact contents.

nodes.title: Dependency Abandonment Risk
nodes.summary: Assess maintainer activity, release health, bus factor, issue responsiveness, takeover signals, and a replacement plan for every critical dependency. This prevents an unmaintained or compromised package becoming an unplanned single point of failure.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect the critical-dependency inventory, recent releases and issue response, maintainer and takeover signals, bus-factor evidence, and a tested replacement plan; record risk acceptance for unresolved items.

nodes.title: API Version Compatibility
nodes.summary: Publish an explicit API versioning and compatibility policy and preserve old behavior until a documented retirement date. This prevents clients from breaking when a removal or semantic change is treated as harmless evolution.
nodes.probe: Present this exact question: “Which versioning and compatibility policy will clients rely on?” Options: “versioned URI,” “versioned media type/header,” or “single backward-compatible contract with documented deprecation.” Require a published policy, support window, and retirement evidence.

nodes.title: API Schema Compatibility
nodes.summary: Maintain a machine-readable API contract and run backward-compatibility checks for every published change. This prevents incompatible field, header, status, and type changes from breaking existing clients.
nodes.probe: Parse current and previous API schemas with a compatibility checker and fail CI on removed or tightened request fields, changed response types, or incompatible status and header changes; include examples for every changed operation.

nodes.title: Bounded Pagination
nodes.summary: Define bounded pagination with deterministic ordering, validated limits, opaque cursors or explicit offsets, and documented continuation metadata. This prevents unbounded scans, timeouts, and duplicate or missing records.
nodes.probe: Request default, maximum, zero, negative, oversized, and malformed page parameters while records change between pages; assert bounded work, deterministic ordering, no duplicate/missing records under the documented model, and valid continuation links.

nodes.title: Problem Details Envelope
nodes.summary: Use application/problem+json with stable type, title, status, detail, and instance members plus a documented field-error extension. This prevents ad hoc client parsing and gives operators a stable failure identifier.
nodes.probe: Trigger representative validation, authorization, not-found, conflict, rate-limit, and server failures; validate content type, required Problem Details members, stable type, safe detail, and field-error shape.

nodes.title: Status Retry Contract
nodes.summary: Document status-code and retryability semantics for each failure class and include Retry-After when a client should wait before retrying. This prevents retries of permanent errors and uncontrolled amplification of transient overload.
nodes.probe: Invoke representative failure fixtures and compare status, Problem Details type, and `Retry-After` behavior against the published retry matrix; assert permanent failures do not request retries and transient failures provide bounded guidance.

nodes.title: Rate Limit Headers
nodes.summary: Enforce documented quota scope and window and emit RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset with a defined 429 response. This lets clients calculate when and how aggressively to back off.
nodes.probe: Send requests past each documented quota from one identity and across identities; parse the three RateLimit fields, 429 status, and reset timing, and assert counters and scope are consistent with enforcement.

nodes.title: Deprecation Lifecycle
nodes.summary: Announce deprecated operations with a replacement, effective date, migration guide, and removal criteria while emitting standardized deprecation or sunset signals. This prevents clients discovering removal only after an outage.
nodes.probe: Invoke every listed deprecated route or field and assert documented `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers, replacement link, and date agree with the API catalog; verify usage monitoring and removal criteria exist.

nodes.title: Mutation Idempotency Key
nodes.summary: Require an idempotency key for externally retryable non-idempotent mutations and bind it to the principal, operation, and request fingerprint. This prevents retries from duplicating charges, jobs, messages, or records.
nodes.probe: Submit the same mutation repeatedly with one key, the same key and a changed payload, and different principals; assert one side effect, replayed result, and deterministic conflict isolation.

nodes.title: Idempotency Atomic Replay
nodes.summary: Persist in-flight and completed idempotency state atomically with the mutation result, define key expiry, and return deterministic conflicts for unsafe reuse. This prevents concurrent duplicates and replay of incomplete outcomes.
nodes.probe: Fire concurrent identical requests and crash or interrupt between reservation and commit; assert a unique key constraint, one committed effect, and a documented replay or retry result after recovery. Reuse the key with a changed payload and assert conflict.

nodes.title: Mutation Atomicity
nodes.summary: Make a mutation's state changes and side-effect intent atomic through a transaction, transactional outbox, or equivalent durable protocol. This prevents partial commits that leave state changed without downstream work.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect mutation transaction boundaries, outbox/event schemas, dispatcher recovery, and reconciliation procedures; verify crashes at each state/side-effect boundary produce no silent partial commit and that duplicate delivery is safe.

nodes.title: Shared State Synchronization
nodes.summary: Identify every shared mutable state location and protect it with a transaction, lock, atomic operation, compare-and-swap, or explicit ownership model. This prevents lost updates, corrupted caches, and nondeterministic results.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect the shared-state inventory and representative read/write paths, then confirm each invariant has a transaction, lock, atomic operation, CAS, or owner boundary; verify lock timeout and failure behavior are documented.

nodes.title: Optimistic Concurrency
nodes.summary: Expose a version or ETag and reject stale writes with compare-and-swap semantics instead of silently using last-write-wins. This prevents concurrent editors or workers overwriting committed changes without detection.
nodes.probe: Read one resource twice, submit two updates using the same version or ETag, and assert exactly one succeeds while the other receives the documented conflict or precondition failure; verify the stored resource contains no lost update.

nodes.title: Race Stress Detection
nodes.summary: Run race detectors, stress tests, and controlled-schedule tests around shared state and make failures reproducible with deterministic seeds. This prevents serial tests from certifying timing-dependent corruption.
nodes.probe: Execute the language's race detector or equivalent stress harness repeatedly with controlled scheduling and fail on race reports, invariant violations, or nondeterministic final state; rerun any failing seed to confirm reproducibility.

nodes.title: Distributed Lock Fencing
nodes.summary: Give distributed critical sections explicit ownership, lease expiry, fencing tokens, and recovery behavior rather than relying on an unbounded lock. This prevents stale workers causing duplicate work or permanent deadlock.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect lock acquisition, renewal, expiry, fencing-token issuance, and protected-write enforcement; simulate a paused owner resuming after lease expiry and verify its stale token is rejected, while a new owner can progress without permanent deadlock.
